description: The Cyber Events Database is a structured record of publicly reported cyber attacks from 2014 to the present, coding each event's date, threat actor, motive, victim, industry and end effects, such as exploitative attacks that steal information and disruptive attacks that interfere with operations. It was created by the Center for International and Security Studies at Maryland and the Center for Governance of Technology and Systems at the University of Maryland to fill a gap in consistent data for decisions on preventing and responding to cyber events. Coverage is global; at access data ran from 2014 to August 2026, with 13,327 events recorded for 2014 to 2023, and since January 2025 candidate events are also found with GDELT news data, improving non-English coverage. The database is available through a web app with visualisations, a download and a codebook, updated monthly, with descriptive information free to the public. Caveats: events come from media reports, so unreported attacks are missing, and a GDELT outage in late June 2025 left an estimated 40 to 60 June records out; the page read gives no licence. For simulation it provides event frequencies and impacts by industry to set cyber attack scenarios for resilience and cascading failure models of finance and other infrastructure. It is related to the Privacy Rights Clearinghouse data breach chronology record in this catalogue.
